description: The portfolio's shared configuration, extended by name. This repository had no Renovate config at all — the bot has been sitting on an unmerged onboarding pull request (#1) since it was installed, which means nothing has been offered here and nothing was skipped either; it simply never started.

What starts now: one Monday batch in UTC, the kotlin / kotlinx / sborka / ci actions groups, the refusal of `kotlinx-datetime:*-0.6.x-compat` (0.8.0 built against the OLD 0.6.x API, which Renovate reads as an upgrade), vulnerability alerts off-schedule, and majors labelled and left to a human.

The sborka group is the one that matters most on day one: the conventions are pinned in settings.gradle.kts and again in the catalog, and without a rule saying they are one release they arrive as two pull requests for one number.

sborka's `automerge-harness` is extended second, so `github-actions` and `gradle-wrapper` updates merge themselves on green — with one exception below. The precondition holds, re-checked 2026-11-25: `ci.yml` and `check.yaml` both run on `pull_request`. The exception is `distributions.yml`, which runs on a tag: `actions/download-artifact` is used there and by no pull request, so it waits for a person. The schedule and automerge were deliberately not adopted in one change; this is the second change.

The actions that only `distributions.yml` uses wait for a person: that workflow runs on a tag (or by hand), no pull request runs it, so a green pull request says nothing about them and a broken one would surface at the next release, not on the merge. Every other action and the wrapper merge themselves through `automerge-harness`, because the pull-request workflows ran exactly those versions.

AFTER the presets, because the last match wins, and in a group of its own: Renovate merges a grouped pull request only when every update in it may merge, so left in `ci actions` these would hold every other action with them. The list is what that workflow uses and no pull-request workflow does (re-checked 2026-11-25); an action added to that workflow later is not on it until somebody adds it here.

The Python of the docs checks. Since #64 it is an input of youndie/docs-bootstrap, not of actions/setup-python, and the github-actions manager reads `python-version` only from actions it knows — so without this rule the 3.14 in check.yaml is a pin nobody moves.
The lookup is the one that manager uses for actions/setup-python (the actions/python-versions releases, npm versioning, the same extractVersion), so the bump arrives exactly as #6 did.
